subject.title: [Bug]: Discord routing / mention-gating issue in OpenClaw

question: Should Discord multi-agent routing suppress the current/default handler whenever a bounded opening attention signal targets another configured Discord bot or role, and should role mentions be wake triggers or only other-mention blockers?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior changes stable Discord routing precedence, role semantics, and bot-to-bot dispatch policy, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Adopt Strict Active-Target Preflight
options.body: Implement bounded attention-window detection and other-configured-bot suppression in the Discord plugin, with role behavior limited to an explicit maintainer-approved contract.

options.title: Keep Default Owner Unless Explicitly Configured
options.body: Preserve current ambient/default-owner behavior by default and add a documented opt-in Discord policy for exclusive active-target routing.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Trackers
options.body: Keep this broad issue open as the umbrella while landing separate fixes for reply-only bots, role triggers, and quoted mention windows.

recommendation.title: Adopt Strict Active-Target Preflight
recommendation.body: Implement bounded attention-window detection and other-configured-bot suppression in the Discord plugin, with role behavior limited to an explicit maintainer-approved contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from current mention-policy history and prior detailed analysis of the related Discord routing precedence issue.
